text:
incident-bot: PAGE: High tail latency observed for tenant 'aurora' on dedicated-pool-7 (VPC). Alert: p95 inference latency > 3s for 15m. Impact: customer requests 10% error, spike in queued requests.

Sana: I'm on it, paging oncall. Any recent deploys to dedicated-pool-7?

ops-bot: Notice: autoscaler triggered +2 instances on pool dedicated-pool-7 at 1954999700.

Liam: no deploys that target that pool. Looking at metrics now — aggregation shows long queue depth and high max_batch_tokens usage for aurora tenant.

Maria: If it's max_batch_tokens hitting upper limits, the scheduler may be allowing very large batches that blow past latency SLO for tail requests. We should temporarily lower max_batch_tokens for that tenant and increase scheduler.smooth_factor to reduce burstiness.

Kevin-CustEng: Aurora reports timeouts on their end, they can route to fallback but want us to keep production running. SLA is strict, customer on Dedicated+VPC.

Sana: Proposed mitigation plan: 1) Apply tenant override: scheduler.max_batch_tokens=1024 -> 512 2) scheduler.smooth_factor +0.2 3) enable queue_shaper.rate_limit=200rps per-tenant soft cap 4) fall back to smaller model variant if latency doesn't improve in 5m.

Liam: I'm preparing the config patch. Will do a canary on pool-7 nodes first.

Maria: Also enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts from aurora — should reduce compute for repeat prefixes. If caching warms, we can relax batch size.

Ryan-Support: FYI sent a note to Aurora: "we're investigating increased latency, making temporary routing changes to protect traffic, will follow up in 10m." They replied: "Thanks — please keep us posted, this is customer-facing search."

Liam: Canary patch below (applied to 2 nodes):
```json
{
  "tenant_overrides": {
    "aurora": {
      "scheduler.max_batch_tokens": 512,
      "scheduler.smooth_factor": 1.3,
      "queue_shaper.rate_limit": "200rps"
    }
  }
}
```

ops-bot: apply-config successful on nodes 7a, 7b.

Maria: Watching latency panels. Also toggled kv_cache.enabled for aurora.

Sana: Metrics update?

Liam: p95 dropped from ~3.6s -> 1.8s after canary. Queue depth down 60%. Error rate trending down but still at 2%.

Kevin-CustEng: Aurora says some requests that were previously hitting 0.8s are now 1.1s, acceptable for them. They asked if we can keep kap prox for next 30m while we monitor.

Maria: Good. Next step: roll the override to full pool-7 (all nodes), keep monitoring, and prepare an automated rollback if throughput drops below target. I'll prepare the revert playbook.

Liam: Rolling to rest of pool-7 now (command: rdmctl apply --pool dedicated-pool-7 --patch aurora-override.json --rollout=immediate).

ops-bot: rollout started, estimated 1m.

Sana: Reminder: update incident doc w/ timeline and customer impact. Ryan, can you keep Aurora updated and capture the reproduction steps they shared?

Ryan-Support: On it. Also capturing sample requests — many very long system prompts, high token counts. Sending redact-safe samples to Eng.

Maria: Noted. If the tenant workload is dominated by very long prompts, lowering max_batch_tokens helps because it prevents the scheduler from aggregating long + short requests into huge batches which create head-of-line blocking. Another knob: per-tenant max_batch_items to limit number of requests per batch. We can set that to 8.

Liam: Applying per-tenant max_batch_items=8 in the same patch.

ops-bot: patch applied to pool-7.

Liam: Post-rollout metrics: p95 ~1.6s, error rate ~0.8%, throughput stable. KV cache hit ratio climbed from 12% -> 44%.

Sana: Good stabilization. Maria, can you create a follow-up task to profile aurora request shapes and recommend longer-term adjustments (quantization profile, smaller model for non-critical routes, or dedicated shards)?

Maria: Will do. Also suggest adding a tenant-specific admission controller that rejects single-request batches exceeding X tokens with a 413 or reroute to async endpoint.

Kevin-CustEng: Customer agreed to a temporary throttling policy for very large prompts while we design a smoother rate plan. They want a post-incident report and timeline.

Sana: OK. We'll keep incident open as "mitigated — monitoring". If p95 holds under 2s and error <1% for next 30m, we'll close.

Liam: Logging the exact commands and diffs in the incident doc.

ops-bot: alert: p95 latency for aurora stable at 1.5s for 10m.

Sana: Thanks all. Handoff to next oncall in 20 minutes: @Maria will own monitoring, @Ryan-Support will manage customer comms. If anything spikes, page the oncall channel.

Maria: Handoff ack. I'll keep watch and start the profiling ticket.

Ryan-Support: Handoff ack. Customer updated.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring.

Sana: Closing notes: root cause likely tenant workload shape (very long prompts) combined with defaults that allowed large batches. Short-term fix: capped max_batch_tokens and max_batch_items, smooth_factor increase, kv cache enable. Long-term: per-tenant admission controller + model-routing and quota guidance.

Maria: I'll turn this into the postmortem draft and include recommended scheduler defaults for dedicated pools handling enterprise tenants.

Liam: Thanks team.

Sana: Closing thread in 30m if metrics hold. :thumbsup:
